  <h1>⚙️ my-vm</h1>
  <p>
    <strong>A high-performance custom Virtual Machine written in Rust.</strong>
  </p>
</div>

## 📖 Overview

**my-vm** is a custom, register-based Virtual Machine built entirely in Rust. It serves as the runtime execution environment for the CVM ecosystem, interpreting `.asm` files generated by the `my-vm-compiler` and providing simulated hardware features like a graphical framebuffer and interrupt handling. It is fully capable of running custom operating systems like `my-vm-os`.

## ✨ Features

- **Register-Based Architecture**: 26 general-purpose registers (`A` through `Z`).
- **Simulated Hardware**: Includes a 1280x800 RGBA graphical framebuffer (with mouse support) rendered via `minifb` — not a classic VGA text-mode buffer.
- **Interrupts Support**: Full support for hardware and software interrupts (`CLI`, `STI`, `IRET`), essential for OS development.
- **Stack & Memory**: Supports standard stack operations (`PUSH`, `POP`, `PUSHALL`, `POPALL`) and direct memory access (`LOAD`, `STORE`) over a large simulated RAM space.
- **I/O Ports**: Features `IN` and `OUT` instructions for port-based communication.

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Rust & Cargo](https://rustup.rs/)

### Building and Running

1. Clone the repository and navigate to the `my-vm` folder.
2. Run the VM, passing an assembly file generated by the compiler:

```bash
cargo run --release -- path/to/program.asm
```

## 🏗️ Ecosystem

This project is part of a larger ecosystem:
- **[my-vm-compiler](../my-vm-compiler)**: The CVM language compiler that generates Assembly for this VM.
- **[my-vm-os](../my-vm-os)**: A custom operating system built to run on this VM architecture.
